name: GraphicsDevice
signature: public abstract partial class GraphicsDevice : IDisposable

docs.summary: Base graphics device. Makes resources, runs commands.
Creates and caches common device resources after creation.
Max in-flight executions.
Start size of each slot's transient bump-allocator buffer, bytes.
Fixed cap on per-execution transient usage, bytes. Over this throws.
Ever-up execution counter. 0 = nothing started yet.
Last known-done execution id. Updated lazily.
Latest GPU-completed execution id. Advances on reclaim. 0 = nothing done yet.
The latest execution id handed out, including one whose recording failed after it began and still submitted work.
Max in-flight executions. Past this, BeginExecution blocks till the oldest finishes.
In-flight execution count. Reclaims finished ones along the way.

Starts a new execution, grabs a free ring slot, blocks on the oldest if all slots are busy.

Replaces the old BeginFrame/EndFrame pair. No "current" execution - the graph builds on this directly.

params.profilers: Profilers for this execution only. Empty creates one from each [`GlobalProfilers`](#api~Prowl.Graphite.GraphicsDevice~GlobalProfilers) factory.

params.profilers: Profilers for this execution only. Empty creates one from each [`GlobalProfilers`](#api~Prowl.Graphite.GraphicsDevice~GlobalProfilers) factory.

docs.summary: Marks execution done; it completes when its GPU work finishes. Non-blocking, stays in flight till the slot's reclaimed. Replaces old EndFrame.
Whether the execution finished on the GPU. Non-blocking. Also polls submissions, so profiler results of finished executions are delivered from here.
docs.returns: True if complete, false if still in flight.

docs.summary: Whether the execution with this id finished on the GPU. Non-blocking, and polls submissions like the task overload.
docs.returns: True if complete, false if still in flight or not yet completed by its dispatcher.

params.executionId: Id of an execution started on this device.

docs.summary: Blocks until the execution with this id finishes on the GPU, or until timeout. Returns false at once if its dispatcher has not completed it yet.
docs.returns: True if it finished before timeout, false otherwise.

params.executionId: Id of an execution started on this device.
params.nanosecondTimeout: Max wait in ns. ulong.MaxValue = no timeout.

members.signature: public bool WaitForExecution(ExecutionTask task, ulong nanosecondTimeout = ulong.MaxValue)

docs.summary: Blocks until the execution finishes on the GPU, or until timeout.

params.nanosecondTimeout: Max wait in ns. ulong.MaxValue = no timeout.

docs.summary: Blocks till all submitted work and in-flight executions are done. Reclaims every slot.

members.signature: public GpuSubmission Record(System.Action<CommandBuffer> record, string name = "")

docs.summary: Records transfer work into a pooled command buffer and submits it now, outside any graph. Only update, copy and mipmap commands are allowed. Wait on the result or drop it for fire-and-forget uploads.
docs.returns: Handle that completes when the GPU is done.

params.record: Records the work. Runs synchronously on the calling thread.
params.name: Optional debug name.

Fires at draw/dispatch when a reflected resource slot has no match and gets a default instead. Null (silent) by default.
Fires on non-fatal warnings, like implicit buffer reallocation. Writes to Console.Error by default; set null to silence, or replace to reroute.
Backend-specific disposal of this device's resources.
True if this device has been disposed.
Frees this device's unmanaged resources. Child resources must already be disposed.

Polls the device's current VRAM budget/usage, as reported by the driver (accounts for other processes sharing the GPU, not just this process's own tracked allocations). False [`IsSupported`](#api~Prowl.Graphite.MemoryBudgetInfo~IsSupported) means the backend or device has no way to report this (e.g. VK_EXT_memory_budget unavailable) - callers should fall back to Counters.Snapshot() ResidentBytes in that case.
Always-on counters of what the backend is doing.
Factories that each create one profiler, or null to skip, for every execution started without profilers of its own.
